name: Template: Infrastructure & DevOps
description: Track incidents and change requests per service from report through verification. Each swimlane is a service or system; each card is an incident or change.

swimlanes.name: API Gateway
swimlanes.notes: Kong API gateway. Handles all external API traffic. SLA: 99.95% uptime.

swimlanes.name: PostgreSQL Cluster
swimlanes.notes: Primary RDS PostgreSQL 15. Read replica in APAC. WAL streaming to S3.

swimlanes.name: CI/CD Pipeline
swimlanes.notes: GitLab CI. Average pipeline: 12 min. Target: < 8 min.

swimlanes.name: Object Storage (S3)
swimlanes.notes: AWS S3. Stores board exports, card attachments, and WAL backups.

swimlanes.name: Kubernetes Cluster
swimlanes.notes: EKS on AWS. Runs all backend services. Auto-scaling 3-12 nodes.

cards.title: Add circuit breaker for downstream DB connections
cards.description:
During last month's DB failover, the API gateway continued routing traffic, causing request queuing and timeout cascades.

Add a circuit breaker that opens after 3 consecutive DB timeouts.

cards.title: Upgrade Kong from 3.1 to 3.6
cards.description:
Kong 3.1 reaches end of life 2026-05-01. Upgrade to 3.6 for security patches and performance improvements.

Breaking changes: plugin API changes in 3.4. Test all custom plugins.

checklist.text: Audit custom plugins for 3.4 breaking changes

comments.body: 2 custom plugins need minor updates for 3.4 API changes.

cards.title: Rate limit bypass on /api/export/ endpoint
cards.description:
Reported by security scan: the /api/export/ endpoint bypasses the standard rate limiter. Large boards can be exported in a tight loop causing elevated DB load.

Severity: P1 — service degradation, not outage.

checklist.text: Confirm rate limit bypass is reproducible
Add rate limiter to /api/export/ in Kong config
Test rate limit enforcement in staging
Verify rate limit is active in production

comments.body: Fix tested in staging. Deploying tonight 02:00-04:00 UTC.
comments.author: demo1

cards.title: Add connection pooling via PgBouncer
cards.description:
During peak traffic (Monday mornings) we approach the max_connections limit. Adding PgBouncer in transaction mode will reduce connection overhead.

Expected: support 2x current peak traffic without hitting the limit.

checklist.text: Migrate app connections to PgBouncer in staging

comments.body: Load test passed. Peak connection count down 68%. Ready for prod.
comments.author: demo1

cards.title: Unplanned failover — primary DB unreachable
cards.description:
2026-03-10 01:47 UTC: Primary RDS instance became unreachable. Failover to replica completed in 4m 22s.

Root cause: AZ-level network event in us-east-1b. Postmortem required.

comments.body: Incident resolved. Postmortem published 2026-03-11. 3 action items.
comments.author: demo1

comments.body: Action items: (1) lower failover time SLA (2) add AZ redundancy (3) page SRE faster.
comments.author: demo2

cards.title: Backend test suite taking 18+ minutes
cards.description:
The backend test suite grew from 8 min to 18 min over the last quarter. Blocking developer velocity.

Investigation: serial test execution, no DB fixtures caching.

checklist.text: Add setUpTestData for fixture-heavy test classes
Verify pipeline drops below 8 min target

comments.body: Parallelization alone cut from 18 min to 11 min. setUpTestData should get us to ~7.
comments.author: demo1

cards.title: WAL backup verification failure
cards.description:
Automated WAL backup verification failed on 3 consecutive days. Backups are uploading but the checksum verification Lambda is timing out.

Actual backups appear intact — this is a monitoring issue, not a data loss risk.

checklist.text: Confirm backups are intact (manual spot check)
Verify verification passes for 3 consecutive runs

comments.body: Backups confirmed intact. Lambda timeout is the issue — fix in staging.

cards.title: Enable S3 Intelligent-Tiering for attachment bucket
cards.description:
Card attachments older than 90 days are rarely accessed. Enable Intelligent-Tiering to automatically move cold objects to lower-cost storage.

Estimated saving: $180/month.

cards.title: Node group OOM kill during Monday traffic spike
cards.description:
2026-03-17 08:45 UTC: 2 backend pods OOM-killed during Monday traffic spike.

Root cause: default memory limit (512Mi) too low for current board query patterns. Increase to 1Gi and add vertical pod autoscaler.

checklist.text: Increase memory limits to 1Gi in deployment manifest
Install VPA and configure for backend deployment
Verify no OOM kills in next Monday spike

comments.body: Memory limits updated and VPA configured. Monitoring next Monday.
comments.author: demo1
